content: 1. A study conducted in Zimbabwe evaluated the effectiveness of an HIV prevention intervention specifically designed for the youth population. The findings were published in the journal AIDS in 2010. 2. Doyle and colleagues investigated the long-term biological and behavioral effects of a community-based adolescent sexual health intervention in Tanzania. This follow-up survey was part of the MEMA kwa Vijana Trial and was published in PLoS Medicine in 2010. 3. Ross and colleagues conducted a community-randomized trial in Tanzania to assess the biological and behavioral impacts of an adolescent sexual health intervention. The results were published in the journal AIDS in 2007. 4. Harper and colleagues examined the impact of increased access to emergency contraception among young adolescents. Their findings were published in Obstetrics & Gynecology in 2005. 5. Franklin and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Sweet Talk, a text-messaging system designed to support young individuals with diabetes. The study was published in Diabetic Medicine in 2006. 6. Chernick and colleagues explored methods to enhance the referral of sexually active adolescent females from emergency departments to family planning services. Their findings were published in the Journal of Women’s Health in 2015. 7. Elliott and colleagues conducted a quasi-experimental study to determine whether untargeted sexual health promotion for young people had reached its limits. The study was published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health in 2013. 8. Funck-Brentano and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of peer support group therapy for adolescents living with HIV. The results were published in the journal AIDS in 2005. 9. Gilmer and colleagues analyzed changes in mental health service utilization when youth-specific programs were offered to transition-age youths compared to adult programs. Their findings were published in Psychiatric Services in 2012. 10. Ngo and colleagues assessed the integration of HIV and sexual and reproductive health services for young people in Vietnam through peer-based education. The project evaluation results were published in PLoS One in 2013. 11. Olson and colleagues developed the Healthy Teens Counseling Approach to change adolescent health behaviors. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2008. 12. Teasdale and colleagues studied the impact of youth-friendly services on the retention of 10–24-year-olds in HIV care and treatment programs in Kenya. The results were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016. 13. Davila and colleagues demonstrated that centralizing HIV services for African-American and Hispanic youth living with HIV improved retention in care. Their findings were published in AIDS Care in 2013. 14. Deogan and colleagues estimated the resource needs for adolescent-friendly health services in 74 lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2012. 15. Kempers and colleagues conducted a cost analysis and exploratory cost-effectiveness study of youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services in Moldova. The results were published in BMC Health Services Research in 2014. 16. Mark and colleagues conducted a situational analysis of HIV treatment and care services for adolescents across 218 facilities in 23 sub-Saharan African countries. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2017. 17. The World Health Organization published a handbook for conducting adolescent health service barriers assessments, focusing on disadvantaged adolescents and their access to universal health coverage. 18. The AIDS-Free Toolkit, developed by the World Health Organization, provides resources for improving HIV prevention, testing, and treatment services. 19. The World Health Organization released technical briefs on HIV and young people who sell sex, inject drugs, or identify as transgender, highlighting their unique challenges and needs. 20. WHO guidelines on adolescent HIV testing, counseling, and care provide implementation strategies for health providers and planners to improve service delivery. 21. Mark and colleagues explored peer support interventions for adolescents and young people living with HIV in sub-Saharan Africa, identifying emerging insights and methodological priorities. Their findings were published in Current HIV/AIDS Reports in 2019. 22. Willis and colleagues evaluated the effectiveness of Community Adolescent Treatment Supporters (CATS) in improving care linkage, ART adherence, and psychosocial well-being among adolescents living with HIV in rural Zimbabwe. The study was published in BMC Public Health in 2019. 23. MacKenzie and colleagues demonstrated that adolescents accessing Teen Club, an adolescent-centered differentiated care model, had greater retention in care compared to those receiving standard care. The study was conducted in Malawi and published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2017. 24. WHO guidelines on mental health interventions for adolescents emphasize the importance of promoting mental well-being and preventing mental health conditions. 25. Mellins and Malee reviewed the mental health challenges faced by youth living with perinatal HIV infection, highlighting lessons learned and ongoing challenges. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2013. 26. Cluver and colleagues conducted a prospective cohort study to assess progress toward the UN Sustainable Development Goals for adolescents living with HIV. Their findings were published in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health in 2019. 27. Laurenzi and colleagues emphasized the urgent need for evidence on preventing mental health conditions in adolescents living with HIV. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2020. 28. Laurenzi and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of psychosocial interventions aimed at improving care engagement and health outcomes for adolescents living with HIV. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2021. 29. Naar-King and colleagues developed Healthy Choices, a motivational enhancement therapy targeting health risk behaviors in HIV-positive youth. Their findings were published in AIDS Education and Prevention in 2006. 30. Chen and colleagues demonstrated that a clinic-based motivational intervention improved condom use among subgroups of youth living with HIV. Their findings were published in the Journal of Adolescent Health in 2011. 31. Bhana and colleagues piloted the VUKA family program, a family-based psychosocial intervention to promote health and mental well-being among HIV-infected early adolescents in South Africa. Their findings were published in AIDS Care in 2014. 32. Bouris and colleagues evaluated Project nGage, a dyadic network support intervention to retain young Black men who have sex with men in HIV care. Their findings were published in AIDS Behavior in 2017. 33. Belzer and colleagues explored the use of cell phone support to improve ART adherence among non-adherent HIV-infected youth. Their findings were published in AIDS Behavior in 2014. 34. Willis and colleagues assessed the effectiveness of CATS interventions in improving ART adherence and psychosocial well-being among adolescents living with HIV in Zimbabwe. Their findings were published in BMC Public Health in 2019. 35. Whiteley and colleagues developed an iPhone game to enhance health outcomes among youth living with HIV. Their findings were published in AIDS Care in 2018. 36. Garofalo and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate personalized text message reminders for promoting medication adherence among HIV-positive adolescents. Their findings were published in AIDS Behavior in 2016. 37. Linnemayr and colleagues found no significant effects of text messaging on ART adherence after one year in a randomized controlled trial among adolescents. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Public Health in 2017. 38. Dulli and colleagues evaluated a social media-based support group for youth living with HIV in Nigeria. Their findings were published in the Journal of Medical Internet Research in 2020. 39. Bermudez and colleagues investigated whether economic strengthening interventions improved viral suppression among adolescents living with HIV in Uganda. Their findings were published in AIDS Behavior in 2018. 40. Christodoulou and colleagues used active visualization techniques to understand medication adherence among youth living with HIV. Their findings were published in AIDS Behavior in 2019. 41. Nestadt and colleagues piloted a family-based psychosocial intervention for perinatally HIV-infected early adolescents in Thailand. Their findings were published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2019. 42. Kaihin and colleagues evaluated the impact of an empowerment intervention on ART adherence among Thai youth. Their findings were published in Behavioral Medicine in 2015. 43. Berrien and colleagues demonstrated that home-based intensive nursing interventions improved ART adherence in HIV-infected pediatric patients. Their findings were published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2004. 44. Brown and colleagues conducted a controlled trial to evaluate the treatment of depressive disorders in adolescents living with HIV. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016. 45. Denison and colleagues assessed the impact of a clinic-based peer mentoring program on viral suppression and adherence among HIV-positive youth in Zambia. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2020. 46. Han and colleagues conducted a systematic review on eHealth literacy among people living with HIV. Their findings were published in JMIR Public Health Surveillance in 2018. 47. Fatti and colleagues evaluated the cost-effectiveness of community-based support for adolescents receiving ART in South Africa. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2018. 48. Brothers and colleagues conducted a pilot trial of a secondary prevention empowerment intervention for young women living with HIV. Their findings were published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2016. 49. Mavhu and colleagues evaluated the impact of a differentiated service delivery model on virological failure among adolescents with HIV in Zimbabwe. Their findings were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2020. 50. Mark and colleagues analyzed data from 324 facilities in 30 countries to optimize HIV service delivery for infants, children, and adolescents. Their findings were published by the World Health Organization. 51. The WHO emphasized the importance of delivering quality health services as a global imperative for universal health coverage. 52. The WHO published recommendations to address stigma and discrimination in HIV care, emphasizing human rights and equity. 53. Kruk and colleagues called for a revolution in high-quality health systems to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Their findings were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2018. 54. The WHO developed standards for quality HIV care, providing tools for quality assessment, improvement, and accreditation. 55. The WHO published consensus guidelines for maternal, newborn, and child health, emphasizing the importance of integrated care delivery.
